method: Nine-name, sector-diversified book built almost entirely from incumbents that re-verified: NVDA/GOOGL/MSFT/AMZN (megacap-tech cluster, 44.8% — under the 48% cap) hold roughly their current weights rather than being added to, since three of the four (NVDA earnings Aug 26, MSFT's live capex/FCF debate, GOOGL's post-rally extension) carry explicit 'don't chase' entry verdicts; AMZN gets the sleeve's largest slot purely on having the cleanest entry (a normal pullback, not chased). LLY and GOOGL are both sized below where their composite rank alone would put them because of vol-scaling. V and MA are new adds, paired at the 20% payments-cluster cap, to refill the Finance sleeve using capital freed by JPM's exit. SPY (20.0%) and VTI (5.0%) are both held essentially flat versus today despite an overbought/near-ATH entry read on the index itself — 'don't chase' argues against ADDING fresh dollars, not against holding the existing, already-appropriately-sized core position. JPM, GE and SHEL are absent from this cycle's verified-survivor set — no adversarial verdict asserting a broken thesis for any of the three was provided, only their exclusion from the research universe's top-10 finalist cut; per the churn governor, a held name missing from the new target without a businessOk:false verdict should phase out over one cycle, not be treated as a hard thesis break. | risk-adjusted (finalize-target.mjs: correlation-cluster + vol-scaled caps) | phase-out retained (churn governor, strike 1): JPM, SHEL, GE

names.thesis: Index ballast (momentum 9.3, uncapped cluster) held flat near its current 20.16% weight — RSI ~83/near-ATH argues against adding fresh dollars here, not against holding the existing, already-right-sized core position.

AWS margin expansion (37% growth, 39.4% margin) is the real driver behind an EPS line distorted by the Anthropic mark-to-market gain; best entry quality (5/10, a normal pullback, not chased) of the megacap sleeve earns it the largest single slot inside the 48% cluster cap.

Azure re-acceleration + top-tier quality/growth (quality 9.3, growth 8.3), held near its current 11.71% weight; FY27 capex guide, a negative-FCF quarter and a pending Copilot-adoption securities suit argue against ADDING into a still-unresolved capex debate.

Second payments-duopoly leg (quality 9.4, momentum 7.5), new add paired with V at the 20% payments-cluster cap; same fee-compression/stablecoin overhang as V but a marginally cleaner entry (no near-term earnings binary).

GLP-1 volume leadership (momentum 8.7, quality 8.7, growth 8.5) sized down relative to its composite rank for the widest 52-wk range in the book plus a chased 89th-percentile entry — thesis intact, sizing reflects price-war margin compression, not a break.

Payments duopoly quality (quality 9.3), new add refilling the Finance sleeve vacated by this cycle's non-survivors; capped with MA at 20% combined given the live DOJ debit-monopolization suit and stablecoin disintermediation debate.

Cloud/AI re-acceleration and top-tier quality (quality 9.2, growth 8.7) offset by the widest 52-wk range of any survivor — vol-scaled below its composite rank; entry set on a pullback, not the current mid-recovery extension.
Small broad-market ballast/parking-vehicle stake held flat near its current 3.13% (rounded to the 5% floor) — same overbought/valuation caution as SPY argues against adding, not against holding.

AI-compute leader (momentum 8.4, quality 9.5, growth 9.7) kept near its current 8.04% weight rather than added to — Aug 26 earnings binary and a bear-case analyst target already at spot argue for sizing the long-run custom-ASIC-erosion risk, not chasing today's price.
